name: Emerald Crystal
reason: Source item 'Blood Jade Crystal' was renamed 'Emerald Crystal' to fit the Western fantasy register; the extraction-from-the-spear and arm-mounting scenes match the source exactly.
description: A powerful crystal Zane extracted from the broken spear Tronson and embedded in his left arm at the Elysian Keep (Ep 142, origin callback in Ep 187). It provides a major power boost and acts as the ultimate counter to enchanted barriers.

name: Adept-level
reason: The source cultivation stage 'Xiantian' was localized as the 'Adept' realm; 'Adept-level' marks warriors and creatures of that tier (Ep 447's 'Consummation of the Adept Realm' matches Ch 434's 'Peak of the Xiantian Realm').
description: A power-tier label for warriors and creatures at the Adept Realm, the localized equivalent of the source's Xiantian stage. Used across the early-to-mid show to rank beasts and fighters (e.g. Adept-level creatures dragged under by Abyssal Pikes in Ep 153).

name: Price
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized: source Li Qiong, the rich merchant of Guanghan Prefecture, became 'Price', a surname that nods to his status as the region's wealthiest man.
description: A wealthy family patriarch in Eps 166-167 whose gate Zane visits; not a petty man, just a father who badly spoiled his only son. Matches source Li Qiong, the richest man in Guanghan Prefecture, who confronts and then placates Luo Zheng after his son is beaten (Chs 152-153).

name: Student ID
reason: The source's sect 'disciple token' was localized as 'Student ID' to match the adaptation's academy-flavored register for the Skyreach Sect (Ep 44's tampering scene mirrors Ch 32's tampered disciple token).
description: The identification item temporary students of the Skyreach Sect receive, obtained by trading in a talisman (Ep 38). It can be drained for power and was once tampered with by an instructor, matching the source's disciple token that Mentor Su secretly altered to spy on Luo Zheng.

name: Hymn of Justice
reason: The source calligraphic killing technique 'Song of Righteousness' (Zhou Dan's trump card, Chs 246-247) was renamed 'Hymn of Justice' to keep the righteous-writing concept in a Western register.
description: Richard's ultimate calligraphic combat technique (Eps 259-260): written characters that radiate golden righteous energy and attack on their own. Zane's corrupt Vitality steadily devours it, mirroring how Luo Zheng's Heavenly Demon True Essence swallowed Zhou Dan's Song of Righteousness in the source.

name: Greater Legendary Beast
reason: The source creature tier 'Super God Beast' was localized as 'Greater Legendary Beast', extending the show's 'Legendary Beast' classification established around Ep 275.
description: The tier above Legendary Beast in the show's creature classification; a single Greater Legendary Beast is a threat even the Cobalt Dragon's Grand Celestial Array in the upper world could only just repel (Ep 514).

name: Karmafire
reason: The source flame 'Hellfire' (karmic fire, as in Pei Tianyao's Green Lotus Hellfire, Chs 303-373) was localized as 'Karmafire', preserving the original's karma-retribution meaning while avoiding religious loan terms.
description: A flame of pure malevolence embodying retribution for mortal sins, contrasted with the Ascended's Voidfire of divine judgment (Ep 315). Patrick's Karmafire is legendary in the Skyreach Sect (Ep 383), matching Pei Tianyao's famed Green Lotus Hellfire in the source.

name: Alistair
reason: The character's Chinese name Ye Qiu was fully localized to 'Alistair Mahoney', an aristocratic-sounding name fitting the arrogant number-one disciple of a rival sect; the episodes use the full name in Ep 355.
description: Nineteen-year-old number-one disciple of the Crimson Sect, winner of The Crimson Crucible, who wields a green middle-grade Mythic Weapon (the Dragon Sword) and has mastered Accomplished Sword Intent (Eps 355-357). He is outclassed and defeated by Finn; matches source Ye Qiu, whose Long Yuan Sword formed Sword Intent cyclones (Ch 343).

name: Cultivation Method
reason: The source's standard term 'cultivation method' was carried over unchanged, consistent with the show's canonical use of 'Cultivator'.
description: The general term for the techniques warriors practice to cultivate, graded by level (e.g. saint-level); warriors channel Vitality through Cultivation Methods to create Magic Circles, and primary methods such as the Malevolent Cycle define a fighter's path.

name: Hidden Test
reason: The source's 'hidden trial' (the secret opportunity concealed in the Burning Heaven Sea of Fire on the Trialtakers' path) was localized as 'Hidden Test'.
description: A secret, access-restricted trial during the sect trial arc (Eps 365-381) that hopefuls tried their luck at but could be barred from entering; corresponds to the hidden trial concealed in the Burning Heaven Sea of Fire in the source's Path of the Trialtakers.

name: Johnny
reason: The character's Chinese name Shangguan Baimeng was fully localized to the casual US name 'Johnny', fitting a brash minor opponent; his 'Iron Hand' nickname directly translates the source's 'Iron Hands'.
description: A disciple famed for his 'Iron Hand' fists, defeated by Zane after Frank's fall (Eps 415-416). Matches source Shangguan Baimeng, nicknamed 'Iron Hands', whose spirit-weapon-hard fists proved useless against Luo Zheng's spirit-weapon body (Ch 402).

name: Julian
issues: NAME COLLISION (merged entity): 'Julian' in Eps 56-61 is Julian Croft, the early Skyreach antagonist who lent the Indigo Blade; 'Julian' / 'Elder Julian' in Eps 439-450 is a completely different character, an elder recruiting for the Dragonblaze Hall in the Upper World. Do not merge their mentions; this row covers the Elder Julian of Eps 439-450.
reason: The Upper World recruiter's Chinese name was localized to 'Elder Julian'; he matches source Zhao Zheng of the Flame Dragon Palace (Chs 425-437), who competed with Elder Wei (Elder Howard) to recruit the protagonist and sent a costly message home. The reuse of 'Julian' collides with the earlier Julian Croft.
description: An elder of the Dragonblaze Hall in the Upper World (Eps 439-450) who, floored by Zane's six-hour mastery of the Laws at the obelisks, tries to recruit him with drops of True Dragon's blood and sends an astronomically expensive message crystal to his distant home hall.

name: Julian Croft
issues: Shares the name 'Julian' with the unrelated Elder Julian of Eps 439-450; keep the two characters distinct.
reason: The character's Chinese name He Bing was fully localized to 'Julian Croft' (masterLS confirms 'NOT Ivan'); like the source's He Bing, he only lends his precious blade to Tristan after being offered a cut.
description: A minor early antagonist (Eps 56-61) who lends his cherished Indigo Blade to Tristan for a share of the winnings, then furiously demands its return after Tristan's defeat; Zane keeps the blade to feed the Cobalt Dragon. Matches source He Bing, who lent his High Grade Xuan Weapon to Xu Lie (Chs 41-43).

name: Graves
reason: The source's unnamed assassin pair, the 'Black White Double Ghosts', were individualized in the adaptation as 'Graves' and 'Roman Stryker' (the 'Diabolic Duo'); 'Graves' was chosen as a grim name fitting a killer shrouded in mist.
description: One half of the Diabolic Duo of mist-wielding killers alongside Roman Stryker (Eps 65-77); their combined power rivaled a Soul Armament, but both died fighting Zane, whose soul-force rendered their black mist useless. Corresponds to the Black White Double Ghosts whom Luo Zheng killed with his broken throwing knife (Chs 58-69).

name: Wrath
issues: Dossier token 'Wrath' is a truncation of 'Wrath of the Ocean' (Eps 1080-1143); it is unrelated to the 'Wrath of Thunder' rune of Eps 522-523 despite the shared first word - do not merge.
reason: The source's special hidden talent 'Jade Gate Immortal Combat' (Chs 1060-1080), a trump card that makes the user's strength soar when activated, was localized as 'Wrath of the Ocean'.
description: A hidden trump-card power manifesting as a pale green stone that flares between the wielder's eyebrows; activating it wreathes the body in blazing golden light and dramatically boosts strength (Eps 1080-1100), matching the source's rare Jade Gate Immortal Combat talent.

name: Wrath of Thunder
reason: The source five-star divine rune 'Fury/Wrath of Thunder Punishment' (Chs 508-511) was shortened to 'Wrath of Thunder' for the sect-protecting array arc.
description: One of the three core divine textures of Cloud Hall's Sect-protecting array (Eps 522-523), delivering devastating offensive strikes that mirror Thunder Tribulation itself; Zane draws it on runic paper alongside 'Light of Water' and 'Frenzied Snare'.

name: Pool of Faith
reason: The source term was kept nearly verbatim: trillions of bits of worshippers' faith converge 'into a pool of faith within the Yao Night Clan' (Ch 1141), localized as the 'Pool of Faith' each queen draws on.
description: The reservoir of worshippers' faith power that each Demon Night queen draws her battle strength from (Eps 1160-1181); sealing off a queen's Pool of Faith, as ordered against Lavender, cuts her from the force that lets the clan's rulers fight far above their cultivation.

name: Supreme Lord Gunter
issues: Episode pronoun signal skews female (m1/f5) because the Queen of Punishment dominates his scenes; the source counterpart (Heavenly Venerate Broken Shadow, m2/f1, 'his son', 'he was once a member of the Elder Assembly') is male - Gunter should be Male.
reason: The source's Heavenly Venerate Broken Shadow, who rose to become the Yao Night Clan's fourth Heavenly Venerate with Yao's help, was localized as 'Supreme Lord Gunter', the Queen of Punishment's staunchest ally ('Supreme Lord' rendering 'Heavenly Venerate').
description: One of the Demon Night's Supreme Lords and the Queen of Punishment's staunchest ally in the late-series political struggle (Eps 1174-1309); countless tiny shadows burst from his body in battle, echoing his source counterpart Broken Shadow Empyrean's shadow powers.

name: Power Transfer
reason: The source ability is named 'Power Transfer' verbatim (Chs 856-864); the localization carried the term over unchanged.
description: Zane's signature defensive ability (Eps 868-1192) that lets him route incoming force harmlessly away - into the earth, the sea, or the world itself - allowing him to withstand blows worth tens of thousands of Dragon Scales; in the source Luo Zheng famously transferred Heavenly Tribulation power into the Heavenly Feather Sacred Sea.

name: Bronze Blood
reason: The source bloodline 'Bronze Blood' (Ch 1189) was kept verbatim; the comparison to the demon race's Berserk Blood also carries over directly (localized as the Ogre race's Berserk Blood).
description: Thane's clan bloodline (Eps 1209-1211), a cousin of the Ogre race's Berserk Blood: once activated it doubles his strength, numbs pain, and drives him into pure thoughtless battle instinct, leaving a trace of green in his dark-red pupils; he pairs it with two Divine Weapon axes.

name: Vitality Pressure
reason: The source's 'pressure of the Yuan Qi' (also rendered 'Vitality pressure' in Ch 1001) was localized as 'Vitality Pressure', consistent with the show's canonical 'Vitality' for the energy.
description: The crushing ambient pressure exerted by the dense Vitality of Heaven and Earth in the Upper World, which every ascended warrior must adapt to (Eps 1004-1026). Zane adjusts in mere seconds - a record that marks him as a monster of talent, echoing the source where only legends adapted within hours.

name: Master Hill
reason: The character's Chinese surname was localized with an initial-preserving Western name: source Palace Master He became 'Master Hill', just as Palace Master Shen became 'Master Sloan'.
description: A master who, together with Master Sloan, escorts Zane to the Myriad Spirit House and watches his exploits there in disbelief (Eps 791-1030); corresponds to Palace Master He, who alongside Palace Master Shen could only warn Luo Zheng during the Spiritual Martial Palace affair (Ch 1005).

name: Elder Roland
reason: The character's Chinese name was localized: source 'Elder Gong' of the Divine Kingdom became 'Elder Roland'; the Ep 734 promise of the internal Scripture of Five Poisons to Simon exactly matches Elder Gong's promise of the inner Five Poison Scripture to Wu Zhanhe (Chs 713, 718).
description: A Life-and-Death Realm elder of a Divine Kingdom (Eps 545-1040) who stands behind its Saintess. After Simon helped her break a curse, Elder Roland repaid him with the internal version of the Scripture of Five Poisons, and he later argues with the Saint Lord over the Thirteen Palaces' recruitment (Ep 1037).

name: Brock
reason: The source's 'Young Master Jing' of the Swallow Cloud Hall was localized as 'Brock', a blunt, forceful name fitting the arrogant genius who tried to strong-arm the protagonist.
description: A powerful and overconfident warrior of Cloudswallow Hall (Eps 1057-1064) who shows up at Zane's manor threatening to take a treasure by force; his source counterpart, Young Master Jing of the Swallow Cloud Hall, was nearly crippled by Luo Zheng's sword over the Thunder and Wind Divine Sword (Ch 1035).

name: Black Mountain Order
reason: The source faction 'Black Mountain Sect' was renamed 'Black Mountain Order', replacing 'Sect' with 'Order' per the adaptation's faction naming conventions (masterLS confirms 'NOT Black Mountain Sect').
description: A fourth-grade power of the Heartlands led by Raven (Eps 453-960), repeatedly appearing alongside Bloodwood Cliff and the Mysterious Luna Hall at major events such as the descent on the Celestial Tomb of Vesper; its heads later bow and smile to Zane after years of friction.

name: Segar Sutton
reason: The character's Chinese name Yu Fei was fully localized to 'Segar Sutton', an unremarkable-sounding name suiting the plain-faced but ruthless tournament fighter.
description: An ordinary-looking Mysterious Luna Hall disciple with a cruel streak (Eps 483-484) who wins the inaugural tournament match by slicing through a barrier with black silk threads, echoing his master's maxim that 'the first battle needs a little blood'. Matches source Yu Fei, whose black silk snaked out at Zhao Dun with the same line (Ch 471).

name: Divine-level
reason: The source talent rank 'god-level' (as in 'god-level genius') was localized as 'Divine-level', the highest talent tier above saint-level.
description: The rarest talent classification in the show, ranking above saint-level (Eps 493-499); Eden Caldwell and Brent possess it, and historically only six Divine-level talents ever appeared across the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms.

name: Trinity Killing Array
reason: The source's triple-kill formation lineage (the 'Minor Universal Triple Slaughter Formation', derived from the 'Major Heavenly Cycle Triple Kill Formation', Chs 511, 719) was localized as the 'Trinity Killing Array'.
description: The sect-protecting formation the Cobalt Dragon taught Zane and that he built for Cloud Hall over nearly two months (Eps 525-736); it hums day and night guarding the sect, and merely possessing it effectively elevates a sect to fifth-grade power status.

name: Fiery Star Flame
reason: The source flame 'Quenching Star Flame' (Ch 527) was renamed 'Fiery Star Flame' for the Western fantasy register.
description: A terrifying flame encountered in the Celestial Tomb arc (Eps 540-549) whose power can be felt before it even arrives; it incinerates Zane's clothes while something within him craves it, matching the Quenching Star Flame that Luo Zheng's golden Sanskrit vortexes hungrily absorbed in the source.

name: Dreaming Marshes
reason: The source location 'Yunmeng Marsh' (also rendered 'Dreamy Cloud Swamp'; 'Yunmeng' means cloud-dream) was localized as 'The Dreaming Marshes', preserving the dream imagery of the original name.
description: The largest swamp in The Heartlands (Eps 546-708), a desolate, fog-shrouded wetland teeming with lurking creatures where the hunted poison master Simon hid from martial artists for years; matches the source's Yunmeng Marsh where Wu Zhanhe took refuge.

name: Bradley
reason: The character's Chinese name Mo Qi was fully localized to 'Bradley', a plain US name for a doomed Peak-tier antagonist in the Tower of Sin arc.
description: A powerful warrior killed by Zane in the blink of an eye in the Tower of Sin (Eps 625-629), his dark blood instantly absorbed by the tower; his fate leaves the War Lord pale with dread. Matches source Mo Qi, the Peak War Elder whose blood and body the Sin Tower absorbed after Luo Zheng tore him apart (Chs 606-607), terrifying Meng Tian.

name: Tide of Chaos
reason: The source phenomenon 'chaotic tide' / 'tide of chaos' (the roughly once-a-decade eruption in the Profound Nether Cave, Chs 623-632) was localized as the 'Tide of Chaos'.
description: A periodic eruption in the Dark Nether Cave region (Eps 642-666) that makes its monsters hyper-aggressive and its inner circle lethally treacherous, driving most factions to retreat to the Tower of Sin; for the bold like Esther, it also opens otherwise inaccessible paths to rare opportunities.
